text:
Maria Choi: Heads up — seeing a short spike of logins that looks like impossible travel + rapid session churn for ~48 accounts in the last 9 minutes. MFA pushes show very high accept rate. Not normal.
Samir Patel: Where are the IPs from? can you paste the query?
Maria Choi: quick query: `SELECT ip, country, count(*) FROM auth.events WHERE event='login' AND ts > now()-interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY ip, country ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 50;`
Maria Choi: top sources: RU, BR, PH, but each IP only 1-3 different accounts. Pattern: same user logging in from multiple countries within minutes (device headers different).
Lee Wong: Could be a proxy farm or VPN churn, or session replay. Any correlation with our SSO provider logs?
Maria Choi: security-bot forwarded Okta audit: multiple `APPROVE_PUSH` events from the mobile prompts. Okta shows pushes accepted.
Jenna Irving: MFA fatigue? Users hitting accept due to notification spam?
Samir Patel: Check if we had any recent RBAC changes or token TTL changes — those can surface weird behavior when session revokes hit different services.
Maria Choi: I checked infra changelog — at 07:12 we rolled out a small RBAC tweak: tightened `session.revoke` permission (PR #4521). It was supposed to be read-only for service accounts but might have altered a consumer that executes bulk revokes.
Lee Wong: That PR touched the internal session-gc lambda identity. If it lost permission, it might not clear stale sessions, leaving old refresh tokens valid while new tokens get pushed — could explain churn.
Samir Patel: Action: I will temporarily disable the session-gc job and run a live revocation for the most affected accounts. Jenna, can you draft comms to ops/security-suppport?
Jenna Irving: On it. Short notice: telling affected users we are investigating unusual sign-ins and forcing password + MFA reset if needed.
Maria Choi: Also seeing KMS audit spikes — a handful of HSM sign requests for the SSO signing key around 07:15-07:22. Might be normal but flagging.
Lee Wong: If key material was rotated or a client used a fallback key, auth behavior could be inconsistent. I'll check KMS rotation logs and key versioning.
security-bot: Incident rule: labeled "sso_improbable_travel_blip", severity P2, alert created #INC-2029.
Samir Patel: Containment plan executed: 07:35 disable external SSO push notifications for the org (temporary config toggle), force-revoked active sessions for the 48 accounts (script: `tools/auth/revoke --ids @list --reason "investigation"`), rotated affected service token for session-gc.
Maria Choi: Confirmed: push notifications stopped, new login attempts dropped to background levels. Some users reported being locked out due to forced revokes — handling via support flow.
Jenna Irving: Comms: posted to #support-status + emailed impacted accounts. Draft to legal and privacy on potential MFA fatigue + account lockouts.
Lee Wong: Post-incident actions I propose: 1) Revert RBAC tweak until we vet the session-gc permissions 2) Add additional Okta webhook validation to detect automated push-accept patterns 3) Add alert when `APPROVE_PUSH` count per user > 3 in 5m 4) Add KMS-side monitoring for unusual signing rate per key version.
Samir Patel: Agreed. Also add a short-run mitigation: rate-limit MFA pushes to one-per-user per 30s and require app-based confirm if more than 2 push prompts in 10m.
Maria Choi: I'll open a follow-up ticket for a focused forensics run: collect full auth traces, device useragent, UA hash, and drop to S3 with retention flag.
Jenna Irving: I'll coordinate with support for user follow-ups and remediation steps (reset, session harden).
Lee Wong: For root cause we need to answer: was this an external abuse (credential stuffing + social engineering) or an internal permission change that allowed stale tokens to persist?
Samir Patel: Timeline so far: 07:12 RBAC PR deploy -> 07:15 KMS sign spike -> 07:20 first unusual logins -> 07:35 containment toggles. We'll need to replay ops logs around 07:10-07:40.
Maria Choi: Tagging infra and devex to help parse telemetry. Also adding an audit requirement: whoever approves bulk revoke flows must now have two-person approval for prod session operations.
security-bot: Added postmortem checklist: collect logs, freeze timeline, assign RCA owner.
Maria Choi: Thanks all. If anyone sees additional anomalies, ping me. Follow-up RFT (RCA ticket): INFSEC-3127. :mag:
